exception_groups.blocker: The control starts, stops, pauses, rescans, or force-terminates owned process work; this read-only census did not manufacture active media work or terminate process trees.
The control persists queue priority, strategy, hold, or manual-order state; the control-only census did not perform persistent queue mutation.
Submitting the rename bad-case form appends a persistent repository corpus entry, which is outside a disposable read-only control census.
The authored launch mirror or backend-initialization-dependent control is intentionally hidden or disabled in the supported disposable state.
The disposable rerun fixture did not contain backend-known issue/bucket dimensions or an imported CSV key required by this control.
The one-row, one-page queue fixture could not create a distinct manual-order draft or another results page.
The disposable queue row already inherited the saved policy and had no saved exact override to clear.
The single-row backend fixture had no detectable series scope, so the series-preview modal and its filters never became reachable.
A non-mutating rename census does not open apply/undo confirmation or result dialogs and therefore cannot activate their controls.

evidence: Exact 352-control census: 286 physical activations, every finite enabled select value, both checkbox states, zero failed or unclassified controls, and no prohibited backend POST. exception_groups.blocker: The local-control census did not invoke backend commands and therefore did not establish the command-specific isolated full-effect preconditions required to credit activation.
The census did not invoke backend persistence and therefore did not establish each command's complete isolated rollback preconditions.
The supported isolated state did not make this backend mutation ready, so the census left it disabled and did not manufacture state to bypass its guard.
The control remained disabled in the supported isolated state because its required upstream selection or mode was unavailable.
This authored control is a hidden derived mirror rather than a reachable operator input in the supported Settings state.
The browser census could not prove the native/backend picker boundary would remain isolated, so the picker did not earn activation evidence.
